The ``parameters`` declaration lists ``dsge_prior_weight``. Dynare refuses: `dsge_prior_weight cannot be declared as a parameter. Use the dsge_var option in the estimation statement instead.`

**Fix**

Remove it from ``parameters`` and pass ``dsge_var`` to the ``estimation`` statement.

codes.title: @#includepath is not a directory
codes.markdown:
### E304: @#includepath is not a directory

The ``@#includepath`` argument does not resolve to an existing directory (a relative path resolves against the root model's invocation directory, including directives in included files). Dynare refuses: `missing_dir does not evaluate to a valid directory`.

**Warrant**

Dynare prints that line inside a `Macro-processing error: backtrace…` block that also repeats the directive and its location; the editor reports the single line.

**Fix**

Point the directive at an existing directory, or create it.

codes.title: @#includepath argument is not a string
codes.markdown:
### E305: @#includepath argument is not a string

The ``@#includepath`` argument does not evaluate to a string. Dynare refuses: `File name does not evaluate to a string`.

**Fix**

Quote the directory: ``@#includepath "mydir"``.

codes.title: load_params_and_steady_state cannot open its file
codes.markdown:
### E306: load_params_and_steady_state cannot open its file

The ``load_params_and_steady_state`` file is not found next to the ``.mod``. Dynare refuses: `Can't open nope.txt`.

**Fix**

Put the file next to the ``.mod``, or correct its name.

codes.title: Trend variable declared twice
codes.markdown:
### E307: Trend variable declared twice

A ``trend_var`` or ``log_trend_var`` name is declared twice. Dynare refuses: `Trend variable A was declared twice.`

**Fix**

Declare each trend variable once.

codes.title: Endogenous variable listed twice as following a trend
codes.markdown:
### E308: Endogenous variable listed twice as following a trend

A ``var(deflator=…)`` list holds the same endogenous variable twice (also across statements). Dynare refuses: `Variable y was listed more than once as following a trend.`

**Fix**

List the variable once.

codes.title: Deflator contains a non-stationary endogenous variable
codes.markdown:
### E309: Deflator contains a non-stationary endogenous variable

The deflator expression of a ``var(deflator=…)`` statement uses a variable that is itself declared with a deflator. Dynare refuses: `The deflator contains a non-stationary endogenous variable. This is not allowed. Please use only stationary endogenous and/or {log_}trend_vars.`

**Fix**

Use a stationary variable or a trend variable as the deflator.

codes.title: Trend variable used outside the model
codes.markdown:
### E310: Trend variable used outside the model

A ``trend_var`` / ``log_trend_var`` name appears outside the ``model`` block (for example in a parameter assignment). Dynare refuses: `Variable A not allowed outside model declaration, because it is a trend variable.`

**Fix**

Use the trend variable in the ``model`` block or as a deflator.

codes.title: filter_initial_state name is not endogenous or exogenous
codes.markdown:
### E311: filter_initial_state name is not endogenous or exogenous

A ``filter_initial_state`` entry names a symbol that is neither endogenous nor exogenous (for example a parameter). Dynare refuses: `filter_initial_state: rho should be an endogenous or exogenous variable`.

The name must have the required type when this row, head, or option is read. Earlier successful `change_type` statements count; later declarations or type changes do not. Repeated macro copies use their own parser context.

**Fix**

List an endogenous or exogenous variable.

codes.title: filter_initial_state exogenous variable without a lag
codes.markdown:
### E312: filter_initial_state exogenous variable without a lag

A ``filter_initial_state`` entry gives an exogenous variable the lag 0. Dynare refuses: `filter_initial_state: exogenous variable e must be provided with a lag`.

The name must have the required type when this row, head, or option is read. Earlier successful `change_type` statements count; later declarations or type changes do not. Repeated macro copies use their own parser context.

**Fix**

Give the exogenous variable a negative lag.

codes.title: filter_initial_state entry declared twice
codes.markdown:
### E313: filter_initial_state entry declared twice

The same ``(name, lag)`` pair appears twice in one ``filter_initial_state`` block. Dynare refuses: `filter_initial_state: (y, 0) declared twice`.

**Fix**

Keep one assignment per ``(name, lag)`` pair in the block.

codes.title: filter_initial_state lag not used by the model
codes.markdown:
### E314: filter_initial_state lag not used by the model

A ``filter_initial_state`` entry uses a lag that the model does not carry: the entry's ``lag`` stands for the model lag ``lag - 1``. Dynare refuses: `filter_initial_state: variable y does not appear in the model with the lag -3 (see the reference manual for the timing convention in 'filter_initial_state')`.

**Fix**

Match an entry's lag to the model: for ``y(-3)`` in the model, write ``y(-2)`` here.

codes.title: optim_weights variable declared twice
codes.markdown:
### E315: optim_weights variable declared twice

One ``optim_weights`` block gives the same variable two weights. Dynare refuses: `optim_weights: y declared twice`.

**Fix**

Keep one weight per variable in the block.

codes.title: optim_weights pair declared twice
codes.markdown:
### E316: optim_weights pair declared twice

One ``optim_weights`` block gives the same pair of variables two weights. Dynare refuses: `optim_weights: pair of variables (y, z) declared twice`.

**Fix**

Keep one weight per pair in the block (the order of the two names matters).

codes.title: Name is not endogenous, or is an exogenous deterministic
codes.markdown:
### E317: Name is not endogenous, or is an exogenous deterministic

A name has the wrong declared role in a slot that requires an endogenous variable, or a `varexo_det` name is used where only plain exogenous variables are allowed. Dynare refuses: `N is not endogenous.` or `N is an exogenous deterministic.` This includes policy `instruments` entries, `std` / `corr` prior and options heads, controlled-path `exogenize`, scheduled shock/path rows, `self`/`prev`/`learnt_in` references, and the older calibration and moment slots. In `estimated_params_remove`, `stderr` needs an endogenous or plain exogenous name and `corr` needs two of the same role. Policy instruments use the type when their command is parsed; a later `change_type` does not validate an earlier instrument. Undeclared instruments use E101.

**Warrant**

For policy instruments, the editor highlights the instrument name; Dynare marks the enclosing command.

**Fix**

Use `var` for an endogenous slot and `varexo` for a plain exogenous slot. Declare or retype a policy instrument before its command.

codes.title: Two ramsey_constraints for one variable
codes.markdown:
### E318: Two ramsey_constraints for one variable

``ramsey_constraints`` constrains the same endogenous variable twice (also across blocks). Dynare refuses: `The ramsey_constraints block contains two constraints for variable y`.

**Fix**

Merge the bounds into one constraint, such as ``0 < y < 1``.

codes.title: Ramsey constraint is not an inequality
codes.markdown:
### E319: Ramsey constraint is not an inequality

A ``ramsey_constraints`` entry is not an inequality. Dynare refuses: `Ramsey constraint has an incorrect form: This expression is not an inequality`.

**Warrant**

For an equality such as `y=0`, Dynare instead stops at the generic `unexpected EQUAL` syntax error. The editor keeps the existing non-inequality sentence to identify the constraint form that needs repair.

**Fix**

Write ``y > bound``, ``y < bound``, or ``lower < y < upper``.

codes.title: Ramsey constraint bound is not constant
codes.markdown:
### E320: Ramsey constraint bound is not constant

A ``ramsey_constraints`` bound holds an endogenous or exogenous variable. Dynare refuses: `Ramsey constraint has an incorrect form: Bounds must not contain any endogenous or exogenous variable`.

**Fix**

Use constants (parameters are allowed) for the bounds.

codes.title: Ramsey constraint does not match the complementarity form
codes.markdown:
### E321: Ramsey constraint does not match the complementarity form

A ``ramsey_constraints`` entry is an inequality but not one of the accepted shapes, and Dynare reports it without a detail. Dynare refuses: `Ramsey constraint has an incorrect form:`.

**Fix**

Write ``y > bound``, ``y < bound``, or ``lower < y < upper`` around a single contemporaneous endogenous variable.

codes.title: external_function without a name option
codes.markdown:
### E322: external_function without a name option

An ``external_function`` statement has no ``name`` option. Dynare refuses: `The 'name' option must be passed to external_function().`

**Warrant**

For an empty option list, an empty `name=` followed by `)`, or an unknown option word, Dynare stops at a generic syntax error. The editor keeps the existing missing-name sentence on these shapes to point at the required function name.

**Fix**

Add ``name='myfunc'``.

**Range warrant**

The missing-name branch selects the `external_function` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: external_function name option without an argument
codes.markdown:
### E323: external_function name option without an argument

The ``name`` option of ``external_function`` is empty. Dynare refuses: `An argument must be passed to the 'name' option of the external_function() statement.`

**Fix**

Pass the function name: ``name='myfunc'``.

codes.title: external_function second derivative without the first
codes.markdown:
### E324: external_function second derivative without the first

``second_deriv_provided=…`` names a derivative function while the statement does not provide a first derivative. Dynare refuses: `If the second derivative is provided to the external_function command, the first derivative must also be provided.`

**Fix**

Add ``first_deriv_provided=…``, or drop the second derivative.

codes.title: external_function bare second derivative without a bare first
codes.markdown:
### E325: external_function bare second derivative without a bare first

A bare ``second_deriv_provided`` asks the top-level function for the second derivative while the first derivative comes from somewhere else. Dynare refuses: `If the second derivative is provided in the top-level function, the first derivative must also be provided in that function.`

**Fix**

Add a bare ``first_deriv_provided``, or name the second-derivative function.

codes.title: external_function nargs differs from an earlier statement
codes.markdown:
### E326: external_function nargs differs from an earlier statement

A second ``external_function`` statement for the same function passes a different number of arguments. Dynare refuses: `The number of arguments passed to the external_function() statement do not match the number of arguments passed to a previous call or declaration of the top-level function.`

**Fix**

Give the statements the same ``nargs``.

codes.title: external_function first derivative differs from an earlier statement
codes.markdown:
### E327: external_function first derivative differs from an earlier statement

A second ``external_function`` statement for the same function names a different first-derivative function. Dynare refuses: `The first derivative function passed to the external_function() statement does not match the first derivative function passed to a previous call or declaration of the top-level function.`

**Fix**

Repeat the earlier ``first_deriv_provided`` form.

codes.title: external_function second derivative from another function
codes.markdown:
### E328: external_function second derivative from another function

The first derivative comes from the top-level function while ``second_deriv_provided`` names a different external function. Dynare refuses: `If the first derivative is provided by the top-level function, the second derivative cannot be provided by any other external function.`

**Fix**

Provide the second derivative in the same function (a bare ``second_deriv_provided``), or name a first-derivative function.

codes.title: init2shocks duplicate endogenous variable
codes.markdown:
### E329: init2shocks duplicate endogenous variable

An ``init2shocks`` block pairs the same endogenous variable twice. Dynare refuses: `Init2shocks(default): enogenous variable 'y' appears more than once in the init2shocks statement` (their spelling).

**Fix**

Keep one pair per endogenous variable.

codes.title: init2shocks first name is not endogenous
codes.markdown:
### E330: init2shocks first name is not endogenous

The first name of an ``init2shocks`` pair is not an endogenous variable. Dynare refuses: `init2shocks: rho should be an endogenous variable`.

The name must have the required type when this row, head, or option is read. Earlier successful `change_type` statements count; later declarations or type changes do not. Repeated macro copies use their own parser context.

**Fix**

Put an endogenous variable first.

codes.title: init2shocks second name is not exogenous
codes.markdown:
### E331: init2shocks second name is not exogenous

The second name of an ``init2shocks`` pair is not a ``varexo`` variable; ``varexo_det`` does not count here. Dynare refuses: `init2shocks: rho should be an exogenous variable`.

The name must have the required type when this row, head, or option is read. Earlier successful `change_type` statements count; later declarations or type changes do not. Repeated macro copies use their own parser context.

**Fix**

Put a ``varexo`` variable second.

codes.title: homotopy_setup name is not a parameter or exogenous variable
codes.markdown:
### E332: homotopy_setup name is not a parameter or exogenous variable

A ``homotopy_setup`` row names a symbol that is neither a parameter, a ``varexo``, nor a ``varexo_det`` variable. Dynare refuses: `homotopy_val: y should be a parameter or exogenous variable`.

The name must have the required type when this row, head, or option is read. Earlier successful `change_type` statements count; later declarations or type changes do not. Repeated macro copies use their own parser context.

**Fix**

Use a parameter or an exogenous variable.

codes.title: shock_groups member is not exogenous
codes.markdown:
### E333: shock_groups member is not exogenous

A ``shock_groups`` member is not a ``varexo`` variable; ``varexo_det`` does not count here. Dynare refuses: `shock_groups: rho should be an exogenous variable`.

The name must have the required type when this row, head, or option is read. Earlier successful `change_type` statements count; later declarations or type changes do not. Repeated macro copies use their own parser context.

**Fix**

List ``varexo`` variables.

codes.title: external_function Jacobian and Hessian from the same non-top-level function
codes.markdown:
### E334: external_function Jacobian and Hessian from the same non-top-level function

The Jacobian and the Hessian are provided by the same external function, but that function is not the statement's top-level function. Dynare refuses: `If the Jacobian and Hessian are provided by the same function, that function must be the top-level function.`

**Fix**

Provide both derivatives in the top-level function (bare ``first_deriv_provided`` / ``second_deriv_provided``), or name two different external functions.

codes.title: Equation-surgery tag matched no equation
codes.markdown:
### E335: Equation-surgery tag matched no equation

A ``model_remove`` / ``model_replace`` tag set names no equation of the model. Dynare refuses: `model_remove/model_replace/exclude_eqs/include_eqs: The equations specified by <tag list> were not found.`

**Fix**

Check the tag value against the ``[name='...']`` tags of the model block, or drop the tag.

codes.title: Excluded equation has no single endogenous on its left side
codes.markdown:
### E336: Excluded equation has no single endogenous on its left side

``model_remove`` removed an equation that carries no ``endogenous`` tag and whose left side is not one endogenous variable. Dynare refuses: `Equation N has been excluded but it does not have a single variable on its left-hand side or an `endogenous` tag`. ``model_replace`` does not gate on this.

**Fix**

Name the variable with an ``endogenous='name'`` tag, or put a single endogenous variable on the left side.

codes.title: Same endogenous excluded twice by one statement
codes.markdown:
### E337: Same endogenous excluded twice by one statement

One ``model_remove`` / ``model_replace`` statement excluded two equations that name the same endogenous. Dynare refuses: `Variable c was excluded twice via a model_remove or model_replace statement, or via the include_eqs or exclude_eqs option`.

**Warrant**

Dynare looks the printed name up at the loop index, so it can name a symbol that was not excluded at all; the editor names the variable that was excluded twice.

**Fix**

Remove the equation once, or drop one of the tags.

codes.title: data statement without file or series
codes.markdown:
### E338: data statement without file or series

The ``data`` statement carries neither ``file`` nor ``series``. Dynare refuses: `The file or series option must be passed to the data statement.`

**Fix**

Pass exactly one of the two: ``data(file='x.csv');`` or ``data(series=y);``.

**Range warrant**

The missing-source branch selects the `data` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: data statement with both file and series
codes.markdown:
### E339: data statement with both file and series

The ``data`` statement carries both ``file`` and ``series``. Dynare refuses: `The file and series options cannot be used simultaneously in the data statement.`

**Fix**

Keep one of the two.

codes.title: data statement nobs is not positive
codes.markdown:
### E340: data statement nobs is not positive

The ``nobs`` option of the ``data`` statement is ``0``. Dynare refuses: `The nobs option of the data statement only accepts positive integers.` A negative value is a syntax error before this check runs.

**Fix**

Pass a positive number of observations, or drop ``nobs``.

codes.title: ms_estimation without no_create_init, datafile and initial_year
codes.markdown:
### E341: ms_estimation without no_create_init, datafile and initial_year

``ms_estimation`` was written without ``no_create_init`` and without one of ``datafile`` / ``initial_year``. Dynare refuses: `If you do not pass no_create_init to ms_estimation, you must pass the datafile and initial_year options.` One sentence covers every missing combination.

**Fix**

Add ``no_create_init``, or pass both ``datafile`` and ``initial_year``.

**Range warrant**

Missing command requirements select the `ms_estimation` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: conditional_forecast without parameter_set
codes.markdown:
### E342: conditional_forecast without parameter_set

``conditional_forecast`` was written without the ``parameter_set`` option. Dynare refuses: ``You must pass the `parameter_set` option to conditional_forecast``. The option takes one of ``prior_mode``, ``prior_mean``, ``posterior_mean``, ``posterior_mode``, ``posterior_median``, ``mle_mode`` or ``calibration``.

**Fix**

Pass ``parameter_set=calibration`` (or the prior or posterior set you intend).

**Range warrant**

Missing command requirements select the `conditional_forecast` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: Scheduled shock or conditional forecast counts differ
codes.markdown:
### E343: Scheduled shock or conditional forecast counts differ

A deterministic `shocks`/`mshocks` row or `conditional_forecast_paths` row lists a different number of `periods` and values. Dynare refuses: `shocks/conditional_forecast_paths: variable Pie: number of periods is different from number of shock values`. A range such as `1:4` counts as one entry.

**Fix**

Give one value per period entry.

codes.title: Scheduled shock or conditional forecast variable repeated
codes.markdown:
### E344: Scheduled shock or conditional forecast variable repeated

One `var` name appears twice in a single deterministic `shocks`/`mshocks` or `conditional_forecast_paths` block. Dynare refuses: `shocks/conditional_forecast_paths: variable Pie declared twice`.

**Fix**

Merge the two rows into one, or remove the duplicate.

codes.title: markov_switching statement missing a required option
codes.markdown:
### E345: markov_switching statement missing a required option

``markov_switching`` was written without one of ``chain``, ``number_of_regimes`` or ``duration``. Dynare refuses: `A 'chain' option must be passed to the 'markov_switching' statement.` with the missing option named.

**Fix**

Pass the named option.

**Range warrant**

A missing chain, regime count, or duration selects the `markov_switching` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: markov_switching chain is zero
codes.markdown:
### E346: markov_switching chain is zero

The ``chain`` option of ``markov_switching`` is ``0``. Dynare refuses: `The value passed to the chain option must be greater than zero.` A negative value is a syntax error before this check runs.

**Fix**

Chains are numbered from 1, in file order.

codes.title: markov_switching number_of_regimes is zero
codes.markdown:
### E347: markov_switching number_of_regimes is zero

The ``number_of_regimes`` option of ``markov_switching`` is ``0``. Dynare refuses: `The value passed to the number_of_regimes option must be greater than zero.` A negative value is a syntax error before this check runs.

**Fix**

Pass a positive number of regimes.

codes.title: markov_switching chain is not the next consecutive integer
codes.markdown:
### E348: markov_switching chain is not the next consecutive integer

The ``chain`` options of the file's ``markov_switching`` statements must be ``1``, ``2``, ``3``, … in file order. Dynare refuses: `The markov_switching chain option takes consecutive integers beginning at 1.`

**Fix**

Number the statements from 1 with no gaps, in the order they appear.

codes.title: markov_switching parameters names are not parameters
codes.markdown:
### E349: markov_switching parameters names are not parameters

A name in the ``parameters=[…]`` option of ``markov_switching`` is not a declared parameter. Dynare refuses: `Variables passed to the parameters option of the markov_switching statement must be parameters. Caused by: Y`.

The name must have the required type when this row, head, or option is read. Earlier successful `change_type` statements count; later declarations or type changes do not. Repeated macro copies use their own parser context.

**Fix**

List only ``parameters`` names, or declare the name as a parameter.

codes.title: markov_switching restrictions row is not three entries
codes.markdown:
### E350: markov_switching restrictions row is not three entries

A row of the ``restrictions`` option of ``markov_switching`` does not hold exactly three entries. Dynare refuses: `restrictions in the subsample statement must be specified in the form [current_period_regime, next_period_regime, transition_probability]`.

**Fix**

Write each row as ``[from_regime, to_regime, probability]``.

codes.title: markov_switching restriction regime above number_of_regimes
codes.markdown:
### E351: markov_switching restriction regime above number_of_regimes

A regime number in the ``restrictions`` option is larger than ``number_of_regimes``. Dynare refuses: `the regimes specified in the restrictions option must be <= the number of regimes specified in the number_of_regimes option`.

**Fix**

Correct the regime numbers, or raise ``number_of_regimes``.

codes.title: markov_switching restriction given twice for one regime pair
codes.markdown:
### E352: markov_switching restriction given twice for one regime pair

Two rows of the ``restrictions`` option name the same ``[from, to]`` regime pair. Dynare refuses: `two restrictions were given for: 1, 2`.

**Fix**

Keep one row per regime pair.

codes.title: markov_switching transition probability above 1
codes.markdown:
### E353: markov_switching transition probability above 1

A transition probability in the ``restrictions`` option is greater than 1. Dynare refuses: `the transition probability, 1.5 must be less than 1`.

**Fix**

Pass a probability of at most 1.

codes.title: markov_switching row or column of transition probabilities does not sum to 1
codes.markdown:
### E354: markov_switching row or column of transition probabilities does not sum to 1

Every transition out of one regime (or into it) was given, and the probabilities do not sum to 1. Dynare refuses: `When all transitions probabilities are specified for a certain regime, they must sum to 1`. One sentence covers both the row sum and the column sum.

**Fix**

Adjust the probabilities so the complete row and the complete column each sum to 1.

codes.title: markov_switching partial transition probabilities sum to 1 or more
codes.markdown:
### E355: markov_switching partial transition probabilities sum to 1 or more

Only some transitions out of one regime (or into it) were given, and their sum is 1 or more. Dynare refuses: `When transition probabilites are not specified for every regime, their sum must be < 1`.

**Fix**

Lower the probabilities, or give the whole row and column.

codes.title: more than one svar_identification block
codes.markdown:
### E356: more than one svar_identification block

The file holds a second ``svar_identification;`` … ``end;`` block. Dynare refuses: `You may only have one svar_identification block in your .mod file.`

**Fix**

Merge the two blocks into one.

**Range warrant**

The range selects the affected `svar_identification` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: svar_identification with both choleskys
codes.markdown:
### E357: svar_identification with both choleskys

One ``svar_identification`` block holds both ``upper_cholesky;`` and ``lower_cholesky;``. Dynare refuses: `Within the svar_identification statement, you may only have one of upper_cholesky and lower_cholesky.`

**Fix**

Keep one of the two.

**Range warrant**

The range selects the affected `svar_identification` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: svar_identification exclusion lag used more than once
codes.markdown:
### E358: svar_identification exclusion lag used more than once

The same ``exclusion lag N;`` opens two elements of one ``svar_identification`` block. Dynare refuses: `lag 0 used more than once.`

**Fix**

Put every equation of that lag under one element.

codes.title: svar_identification equation number repeated under one lag
codes.markdown:
### E359: svar_identification equation number repeated under one lag

Two ``equation N, …;`` rows under one ``exclusion lag`` carry the same equation number. Dynare refuses: `equation number 1 referenced more than once under a single lag.`

**Fix**

Name each equation once per lag.

codes.title: svar_identification equation number below 1
codes.markdown:
### E360: svar_identification equation number below 1

An ``equation`` row of ``svar_identification`` carries the number ``0``. Dynare refuses: `equation numbers must be greater than or equal to 1.` A negative number is a syntax error before this check runs, and the ``restriction equation N, …`` spelling is not range-checked.

**Fix**

Number equations from 1.

codes.title: svar_identification name added twice in one equation row
codes.markdown:
### E361: svar_identification name added twice in one equation row

One ``equation N, name…;`` row lists the same name twice. Dynare refuses: `Py restriction added twice.`

**Fix**

List the name once.

codes.title: svar_identification restriction mixes Qi and Ri
codes.markdown:
### E362: svar_identification restriction mixes Qi and Ri

One ``restriction equation N, …;`` uses both a ``coeff(name,0)`` term (the contemporaneous Qi matrix) and a ``coeff(name,k)`` term with ``k > 0`` (the lagged Ri matrix). Dynare refuses: `SVAR_IDENTIFICATION: a single restrictions must affect either Qi or Ri, but not both`.

**Fix**

Split the restriction into one statement per matrix.

codes.title: svar without coefficients, variances or constants
codes.markdown:
### E363: svar without coefficients, variances or constants

``svar`` was written without any of ``coefficients``, ``variances`` or ``constants``. Dynare refuses: `You must pass one of 'coefficients', 'variances', or 'constants'.` The third name is unreachable at this pin: ``constants`` is a token the grammar does not take, so spelling it is a syntax error.

**Fix**

Pass ``coefficients`` or ``variances``.

**Range warrant**

A missing required choice or chain selects the `svar` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: svar with two of coefficients, variances and constants
codes.markdown:
### E364: svar with two of coefficients, variances and constants

``svar`` was written with two of ``coefficients``, ``variances`` and ``constants``. Dynare refuses: `You may only pass one of 'coefficients', 'variances', or 'constants'.` The third name is unreachable at this pin: ``constants`` is a token the grammar does not take, so spelling it is a syntax error.

**Fix**

Keep one of the two.

codes.title: svar without the chain option
codes.markdown:
### E365: svar without the chain option

``svar`` was written without the ``chain`` option. Dynare refuses: `A 'chain' option must be passed to the 'svar' statement.`

**Fix**

Pass ``chain=N``; the number must name the matching ``markov_switching`` chain.

**Range warrant**

A missing required choice or chain selects the `svar` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: svar chain is zero
codes.markdown:
### E366: svar chain is zero

The ``chain`` option of ``svar`` is ``0``. Dynare refuses: `The value passed to the 'chain' option must be greater than zero.` This is a different sentence from the one ``markov_switching`` prints for its own ``chain``. A negative or fractional value is a syntax error before this check runs.

**Fix**

Number the chain from 1.

codes.title: svar equations option holds a non-positive number
codes.markdown:
### E367: svar equations option holds a non-positive number

The ``equations=[…]`` option of ``svar`` holds a number that is ``0`` or less. Dynare refuses: `The value(s) passed to the 'equations' option must be greater than zero.` An empty list and a negative value are syntax errors before this check runs.

**Fix**

Number the equations from 1.

codes.title: ms_compute_probabilities with both probability options
codes.markdown:
### E368: ms_compute_probabilities with both probability options

``ms_compute_probabilities`` was written with both ``real_time_smoothed`` and ``filtered_probabilities``. Dynare refuses: `You may only pass one of real_time_smoothed and filtered_probabilities to ms_compute_probabilities.`

**Fix**

Keep one of the two.

codes.title: ms_irf with more than one regime or probability option
codes.markdown:
### E369: ms_irf with more than one regime or probability option

``ms_irf`` was written with more than one of ``regime``, ``regimes`` and ``filtered_probabilities``. Dynare refuses: `You may only pass one of regime, regimes and filtered_probabilities to ms_irf`. No full stop.

**Fix**

Keep one of the three.

codes.title: ms_forecast with both regime and regimes
codes.markdown:
### E370: ms_forecast with both regime and regimes

``ms_forecast`` was written with both ``regime`` and ``regimes``. Dynare refuses: `You may only pass one of regime and regimes to ms_forecast`. No full stop. ``ms_forecast`` has no ``filtered_probabilities`` option.

**Fix**

Keep one of the two.

codes.title: ms_variance_decomposition with more than one regime or probability option
codes.markdown:
### E371: ms_variance_decomposition with more than one regime or probability option

``ms_variance_decomposition`` was written with more than one of ``regime``, ``regimes`` and ``filtered_probabilities``. Dynare refuses: `You may only pass one of regime, regimes and filtered_probabilities to ms_variance_decomposition`. No full stop.

**Fix**

Keep one of the three.

codes.title: prior statement without the shape option
codes.markdown:
### E372: prior statement without the shape option

A dotted ``prior`` statement carries no ``shape``. Dynare refuses: `You must pass the shape option to the prior statement.` The sentence is the same for the plain, ``std(…)``, ``corr(…)`` and joint forms.

**Fix**

Pass ``shape=beta`` (or the distribution you intend).

**Range warrant**

The range selects the dotted statement's `prior` keyword, rather than the target name. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: prior statement without mean or mode
codes.markdown:
### E373: prior statement without mean or mode

A dotted ``prior`` statement carries neither ``mean`` nor ``mode``. Dynare refuses: `You must pass at least one of mean and mode to the prior statement.` Passing both is accepted.

**Fix**

Pass ``mean=`` or ``mode=``.

**Range warrant**

The range selects the dotted statement's `prior` keyword, rather than the target name. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: prior statement without exactly one of stdev and variance
codes.markdown:
### E374: prior statement without exactly one of stdev and variance

A dotted ``prior`` statement carries neither ``stdev`` nor ``variance``, or both. Dynare refuses: `You must pass exactly one of stdev and variance to the prior statement.` One sentence covers both cases; the joint ``[a, b]`` form is not checked.

**Fix**

Pass exactly one of the two.

**Range warrant**

When neither variance option is present, the range selects the dotted statement's `prior` keyword. When both are present, it keeps the existing range. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: prior statement domain does not hold two values
codes.markdown:
### E375: prior statement domain does not hold two values

The ``domain`` option of a single ``prior`` statement does not hold exactly two values. Dynare refuses: `You must pass exactly two values to the domain option.` An empty list is a syntax error before this check runs.

**Fix**

Pass two values, such as ``domain=[0, 1]``.

codes.title: joint prior statement domain does not hold four values
codes.markdown:
### E376: joint prior statement domain does not hold four values

The ``domain`` option of a joint ``[a, b].prior(…)`` statement does not hold exactly four values. Dynare refuses: `You must pass exactly four values to the domain option.`

**Fix**

Pass four values, such as ``domain=[0.1 0.2 0.3 0.4]``.

codes.title: joint prior statement with fewer than two names
codes.markdown:
### E377: joint prior statement with fewer than two names

A joint prior statement names fewer than two parameters. Dynare refuses: `you must pass at least two parameters to the joint prior statement`. The lowercase ``you`` is theirs.

**Fix**

Name two or more parameters, or use the single ``name.prior(…)`` form.

**Range warrant**

The range selects the joint statement's `prior` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: Name is not a parameter
codes.markdown:
### E378: Name is not a parameter

A top-level `symbol = …;` assignment, or the head of a plain or bracketed ``prior`` or plain ``options`` statement, names a symbol that is not a parameter. Dynare refuses while parsing with `y is not a parameter`. Named subsample heads use the same test. `discretionary_policy` initializes `optimal_policy_discount_factor` before validating instruments and requires that name to be a parameter at the command. A later `change_type` does not validate an earlier initialization. The ``std(…)`` and ``corr(…)`` heads print their own sentence instead, and a line whose head the file never declares is native MATLAB text that 7.2 accepts.

**Fix**

Name a ``parameters`` symbol, or move the statement to the surface that takes this kind.

codes.title: corr prior or options mixes an endogenous and an exogenous name
codes.markdown:
### E379: corr prior or options mixes an endogenous and an exogenous name

The two names of a ``corr(A,B).prior(…)`` or ``corr(A,B).options(…)`` statement are of different types. Dynare refuses: `In the corr(A,B).prior statement, A and B must be of the same type. In your case, Pie and eps are of different types.` The options form uses `corr(A,B).options` in that sentence.

**Fix**

Name two endogenous variables or two exogenous ones.

codes.title: load_params_and_steady_state names an unsupported variable type
codes.markdown:
### E380: load_params_and_steady_state names an unsupported variable type

The data file of ``load_params_and_steady_state`` holds a name that is declared, but not as a parameter, an endogenous variable, a ``varexo``, or a ``varexo_det``: an ``epilogue`` helper, an ``external_function`` name, or a trend variable. The checks accept this unsupported-type entry. While writing the MATLAB files, Dynare refuses: `Unsupported variable type for A in load_params_and_steady_state`.

**Warrant**

For a used trend that breaks balanced growth, Dynare's earlier Compute test prints its cross-partial refusal and hides the writer sentence. The editor still reports this written-file loader error; checking balanced growth would require the Compute work it does not perform.

**Fix**

Remove the entry from the data file, or name one of the four allowed kinds.

codes.title: steady_state operator contains an external function
codes.markdown:
### E381: steady_state operator contains an external function

The expression inside a ``steady_state(…)`` operator calls an ``external_function``. Dynare accepts the file through its checks and refuses only when writing the MATLAB files: `The expression inside a steady_state operator cannot contain external functions`.

**Fix**

Move the call out of the ``steady_state(…)`` operator.

codes.title: method_of_moments without a method
codes.markdown:
### E382: method_of_moments without a method

A ``method_of_moments`` statement carries no ``mom_method`` option, so Dynare cannot tell GMM, SMM, and IRF matching apart. Dynare refuses: `The 'method_of_moments' statement requires a method to be supplied via the 'mom_method' option. Possible values are 'GMM', 'SMM', or 'IRF_MATCHING'.`

The option value must be one of those three bare words; a quoted or other word is a syntax error, reported as **E001**.

**Fix**

Add ``mom_method=GMM``, ``mom_method=SMM``, or ``mom_method=IRF_MATCHING``.

**Range warrant**

The missing requirement selects the `method_of_moments` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: method_of_moments without a data file
codes.markdown:
### E383: method_of_moments without a data file

A ``method_of_moments`` statement asks for ``GMM`` or ``SMM`` but names no ``datafile``. Both methods match moments against data, so the file is required. Dynare refuses: `The 'method_of_moments' statement requires a data file to be supplied via the 'datafile' option.`

``IRF_MATCHING`` does not need one. The file itself need not exist yet at this step; a named one that is missing is **W160**.

**Fix**

Add ``datafile='your_data.csv'``.

**Range warrant**

The missing requirement selects the `method_of_moments` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: analytic option without GMM
codes.markdown:
### E384: analytic option without GMM

``analytic_standard_errors`` or ``analytic_jacobian`` is a bare flag on a ``method_of_moments`` statement whose ``mom_method`` is ``SMM`` or ``IRF_MATCHING``. Only GMM has the analytic derivatives these options ask for. Dynare refuses: `The analytic_standard_errors statement requires the GMM option.` (or ``analytic_jacobian`` in place of the first name).

**Fix**

Drop the option, or switch ``mom_method`` to ``GMM``.

codes.title: method_of_moments with more than one filter
codes.markdown:
### E385: method_of_moments with more than one filter

A ``method_of_moments`` statement asks for more than one of ``hp_filter``, ``one_sided_hp_filter``, and ``bandpass_filter``. Dynare refuses: `method_of_moments: can only use one of HP, one-sided HP, and bandpass filters`

This is the ``method_of_moments`` sentence; ``stoch_simul`` has its own (**E238**).

**Fix**

Keep one filter.

codes.title: Matched moment is not a supported shape
codes.markdown:
### E386: Matched moment is not a supported shape

A ``matched_moments`` row is not a shape the moment matcher accepts. Dynare refuses: `Matched moment expression has incorrect format: {reason}`, where the reason is one of:

- `Variable {name} is not an endogenous`
- `Unsupported binary operator`
- `First argument of power expression must be a variable`
- `Second argument of power expression must be a positive integer`
- `Unsupported expression`

A moment is a product of endogenous variables, each optionally raised to a positive whole-number power, each optionally with a lead or a lag. So ``y``, ``c*y``, ``y^2``, ``y*y(-1)`` and ``y(1)`` are accepted, while ``y+c``, ``log(y)``, ``1``, and ``y^c`` are not. The reason names the first problem found.

**Fix**

Rewrite the row as a product of endogenous variables with positive integer powers.

codes.title: Name is not exogenous
codes.markdown:
### E387: Name is not exogenous

A name in a plain exogenous slot is declared as another type. Dynare refuses: `{name} is not exogenous.` These slots include scheduled and heteroskedastic shock rows, `shock_paths` targets and controlled `endogenize`, `self`/`prev`/`learnt_in` references, and the shock slots of `matched_irfs` and `matched_irfs_weights`. The `irf_calibration` shock uses Dynare's separate `Variable {endo} is not an exogenous.` sentence. A `varexo_det` name gets its own E317 sentence.

**Fix**

Use a plain `varexo` variable.

codes.title: matched_irfs pair repeated
codes.markdown:
### E388: matched_irfs pair repeated

One ``matched_irfs`` block lists the same endogenous/shock pair twice. Dynare refuses: `matched_irfs: the pair endogenous {y} with exogenous {e} appears two times`. The periods may differ; the pair is the key. Two separate blocks may repeat a pair silently.

**Fix**

Merge the two rows into one, or drop the second.

codes.title: matched_irfs_weights tuple repeated
codes.markdown:
### E389: matched_irfs_weights tuple repeated

One ``matched_irfs_weights`` block lists the same six-part tuple twice: both endogenous names with their periods, and both shock names. The weight is not part of the key, so two rows differing only in the weight are refused. Dynare refuses: `matched_irfs: the tuple ({y}({1}),{e},{c}({2}),{e}) appears two times`, with no spaces around the parts.

**Fix**

Merge the two rows, or drop the second.

codes.title: matched_irfs periods and values counts differ
codes.markdown:
### E390: matched_irfs periods and values counts differ

In one ``matched_irfs`` row the ``periods`` and ``values`` lists hold different numbers of elements. Dynare refuses: `matched_irfs: the 'periods' and 'values' keywords are not followed by the same number of elements`. A range such as ``1:2`` counts as one period, and a parenthesised value such as ``(xx)`` as one value.

**Fix**

Give one value per period.

codes.title: matched_irfs periods and weights counts differ
codes.markdown:
### E391: matched_irfs periods and weights counts differ

In one ``matched_irfs`` row the ``weights`` list holds more than one element and does not match the number of periods. Dynare refuses: `matched_irfs: the 'periods' and 'weights' keywords are not followed by the same number of elements`. A single weight is accepted and copied across the periods.

**Fix**

Give one weight per period, or a single weight for the whole row.

codes.title: matched_irfs periods holds a date
codes.markdown:
### E392: matched_irfs periods holds a date

A ``periods`` entry of a ``matched_irfs`` row is written as a date such as ``2000Q1``. The row counts periods after the start of the simulation, so it takes integers and integer ranges only. Dynare refuses: `matched_irfs: dates are not allowed in the 'periods' keyword`

**Fix**

Write the horizon as an integer, or as an ``a:b`` range of integers.

codes.title: Shock skewness declared twice
codes.markdown:
### E393: Shock skewness declared twice

The same single-shock skewness is specified twice. Dynare refuses: `shocks: skewness of e declared twice`. An ordinary `shocks` block, including `shocks(learnt_in=1)`, clears the skewness entries at its end. Dynare 7.2 retains entries after `shocks(heterogeneity=…)`, so repetition in a following heterogeneous or ordinary block also counts.

**Fix**

Remove the repeated `skew e` row.

codes.title: Shock co-skewness declared twice
codes.markdown:
### E394: Shock co-skewness declared twice

The same three-shock co-skewness is specified twice, even if the names are reordered. Dynare refuses: `shocks: co-skewness of (v, e, u) declared twice`. An ordinary `shocks` block, including `shocks(learnt_in=1)`, clears the skewness entries at its end. Dynare 7.2 retains entries after `shocks(heterogeneity=…)`, so repetition in a following heterogeneous or ordinary block also counts.

**Fix**

Remove the repeated row for the unordered triple.

codes.title: Period range runs backwards
codes.markdown:
### E395: Period range runs backwards

An integer period range starts after it ends. Dynare refuses: `Can't have first period index greater than second index in range specification`.

**Fix**

Put the earlier period first.

codes.title: Ordinary shocks uses add or multiply without nondefault learning
codes.markdown:
### E396: Ordinary shocks uses add or multiply without nondefault learning

An ordinary `shocks` block uses `add` or `multiply`. Dynare refuses: `shocks: 'add' keyword not allowed unless 'learnt_in' option with value >1 is passed` (or `multiply` in place of `add`). `learnt_in=1` follows the ordinary rule.

**Fix**

Use `values`, or use a nondefault `learnt_in` block when the later learning date is intended.

codes.title: mshocks uses add or multiply
codes.markdown:
### E397: mshocks uses add or multiply

A `mshocks` row uses `add` or `multiply`. Dynare refuses: `mshocks: 'add' keyword not allowed` (or `multiply` in place of `add`).

**Fix**

Use `values` in `mshocks`.

codes.title: Surprise shocks uses add or multiply
codes.markdown:
### E398: Surprise shocks uses add or multiply

A `shocks(surprise)` row uses `add` or `multiply`. Dynare refuses: `shocks(surprise): 'add' keyword not allowed` (or `multiply` in place of `add`).

**Fix**

Use `values` for the surprise shock.

codes.title: Surprise shock period is a date
codes.markdown:
### E399: Surprise shock period is a date

A `shocks(surprise)` period is written as a DATE. Dynare refuses: `shocks(surprise): dates are not allowed in the 'periods' keyword`.

**Fix**

Use an integer period or integer range.

codes.title: Shock learning period is below one
codes.markdown:
### E400: Shock learning period is below one

A `shocks` or `mshocks` `learnt_in` option is an integer below one. Dynare refuses: `shocks: value '0' is not allowed for 'learnt_in' option` (with `mshocks` in that block).

**Fix**

Use a positive integer or DATE.

codes.title: Shock occurs before it is learnt
codes.markdown:
### E401: Shock occurs before it is learnt

A written integer shock period precedes the integer `learnt_in` period in `shocks` or `mshocks`. Dynare refuses: `shocks: for variable e, shock period (2) is earlier than the period in which the shock is learnt (3)` (with `mshocks` in that block).

**Fix**

Move the shock period to the learning period or later, or correct `learnt_in`.

codes.title: Heteroskedastic shock row repeated
codes.markdown:
### E402: Heteroskedastic shock row repeated

A `heteroskedastic_shocks` block repeats a variable in the same `values` or `scales` row kind. Dynare refuses: `heteroskedastic_shocks: variable e declared twice`. One `values` and one `scales` row for the same variable are allowed.

**Fix**

Keep one row per variable and row kind in each block.

codes.title: Heteroskedastic periods and values differ in count
codes.markdown:
### E403: Heteroskedastic periods and values differ in count

A `heteroskedastic_shocks` row has a different number of `periods` and `values` or `scales` entries. Dynare refuses: `heteroskedastic_shocks: variable e: number of periods is different from number of shock values`.

**Fix**

Give one value or scale per period entry.

codes.title: Shock path periods and values differ in count
codes.markdown:
### E404: Shock path periods and values differ in count

An exogenous `shock_paths` stanza has a different number of `periods` and `values` entries. Dynare refuses: `shock_paths: variable e: number of periods is different from number of shock values`.

**Fix**

Give one expression per period entry.

codes.title: Shock path lag reaches before its period
codes.markdown:
### E405: Shock path lag reaches before its period

An exogenous `shock_paths` expression uses a lag unavailable at its written integer period. Dynare refuses: `shock_paths: a lag of 1 is not allowed at period 1`.

**Fix**

Move the path to a later period or use a shorter lag.

codes.title: Controlled path periods and values differ in count
codes.markdown:
### E406: Controlled path periods and values differ in count

A controlled `shock_paths` or `perfect_foresight_controlled_paths` stanza has a different number of `periods` and `values` entries. Dynare refuses: `The number of periods is different from the number of values`.

**Fix**

Give one value expression per period entry.

codes.title: Bare shock path name is not a parameter
codes.markdown:
### E407: Bare shock path name is not a parameter

A bare declared name in a `shock_paths` value is not a parameter. Dynare refuses: `In the shock_paths block, parameters are the only symbols allowed without a namespace-qualifier`.

**Fix**

Use a parameter, or the supported namespace for the variable you mean.

codes.title: self reference has a lead
codes.markdown:
### E408: self reference has a lead

A `self` reference in `shock_paths` has a positive lead. Dynare refuses: `The syntax self.u cannot be used with a lead`.

**Fix**

Use the current value or a lag.

codes.title: Namespace lag is not an integer
codes.markdown:
### E409: Namespace lag is not an integer

A `self`, `prev`, `learnt_in`, or declared database reference in `shock_paths` has a lag argument that does not fold to an integer. Dynare refuses: `Symbol self.u is being treated as if it were a function (i.e., passed an argument that is not an integer).`

**Fix**

Use an integer lag expression.

codes.title: Namespace reference has multiple lag arguments
codes.markdown:
### E410: Namespace reference has multiple lag arguments

A `self`, `prev`, or declared database reference in `shock_paths` is called with more than one argument. Dynare refuses: `The parenthesis after self.u should only include a lag, since it references a variable inside a namespace`.

**Fix**

Pass one integer lag.

codes.title: prev reference requires a later learning period
codes.markdown:
### E411: prev reference requires a later learning period

A `prev` reference appears in a default `shock_paths` block or `learnt_in=1`. Dynare refuses: `The syntax prev.u is not accepted in a 'shock_paths' block without the 'learnt_in' option or in a 'shock_paths(learnt_in=1)' block`.

**Fix**

Use a later integer or DATE `learnt_in`, or another supported reference.

codes.title: learnt_in reference period is below one
codes.markdown:
### E412: learnt_in reference period is below one

A `learnt_in(…)` path reference uses an integer below one. Dynare refuses: `The syntax learnt_in(0).u is not accepted`.

**Fix**

Use a positive informational period.

codes.title: learnt_in reference is not earlier than the path learning period
codes.markdown:
### E413: learnt_in reference is not earlier than the path learning period

When both learning periods are integers, a `learnt_in(…)` reference must name an earlier period than the `shock_paths` block. Dynare refuses: `The syntax learnt_in(2).u is not accepted in a 'shock_paths' block without the 'learnt_in' option or in a 'shock_paths(learnt_in=2)' block`. Dynare does not make this integer comparison for DATE values at this stage.

**Fix**

Use an earlier integer period in the reference.

codes.title: Database declared twice
codes.markdown:
### E414: Database declared twice

A `database` name is declared again. Dynare refuses: `Database 'db' already declared`.

**Fix**

Declare each database name once.

codes.title: Shock path refers to an unknown database
codes.markdown:
### E415: Shock path refers to an unknown database

A bare `db.x` reference in `shock_paths` names a database not declared earlier. Dynare refuses: `Unknown database: db. You may want to declare it via the 'database' command.` An unknown `db.x(1)` is parsed as a function call instead.

**Fix**

Declare the database before the path, or correct its name.

codes.title: Namespace reference in a controlled path
codes.markdown:
### E416: Namespace reference in a controlled path

A controlled `shock_paths` stanza uses `self`, `prev`, `learnt_in`, or a database namespace in its value. Dynare refuses: `The syntax self.e is not accepted in an 'endogenize' stanza of a 'shock_paths' block`.

**Fix**

Use a plain expression or an allowed `initval`/`init` reference.

codes.title: endval change operation needs nondefault learning
codes.markdown:
### E417: endval change operation needs nondefault learning

An `endval` row uses `+=` or `*=` without `learnt_in>1` or a DATE. Dynare refuses: `endval: 'e += ...' line not allowed unless 'learnt_in' option with value >1 or date is passed` (or `*=` in place of `+=`).

**Fix**

Use `=`, or set the intended later `learnt_in`.

codes.title: endval learning period is below one
codes.markdown:
### E418: endval learning period is below one

An `endval` `learnt_in` option is an integer below one. Dynare refuses: `endval: value '0' is not allowed for 'learnt_in' option`.

**Fix**

Use a positive integer or DATE.

codes.title: endval learnt-in row is not exogenous
codes.markdown:
### E419: endval learnt-in row is not exogenous

A nondefault `endval(learnt_in=…)` row names something other than a plain exogenous variable. Dynare refuses: `endval(learnt_in=...): y is not an exogenous variable`.

**Fix**

Use a `varexo` name, or put the intended assignment in an ordinary `endval` block.

codes.title: Shock path refers to itself at lag zero
codes.markdown:
### E420: Shock path refers to itself at lag zero

A path for `e` uses `self.e` without a lag or at lag zero. Dynare refuses: `in the definition of 'e' in a 'shock_paths' block, the use of 'self.e' without a lag is not allowed, since it is a circular reference`. `self.u` at zero is allowed in a path for `e`.

**Fix**

Use a lagged `self.e` or another variable.

codes.title: Path learning period is below one
codes.markdown:
### E421: Path learning period is below one

A `shock_paths` or `perfect_foresight_controlled_paths` `learnt_in` option is an integer below one. Dynare refuses: `Value '0' is not allowed for 'learnt_in' option`.

**Fix**

Use a positive integer or DATE.

codes.title: Learnt-in shocks need expectation-errors commands
codes.markdown:
### E422: Learnt-in shocks need expectation-errors commands

A nondefault `shocks(learnt_in=…)` or `mshocks(learnt_in=…)` block needs both expectation-errors setup and solver, without regular perfect-foresight setup or solver. Dynare refuses: `the 'shocks(learnt_in=…)' block can only be used in conjunction with the 'perfect_foresight_with_expectation_errors_setup' and 'perfect_foresight_with_expectation_errors_solver' commands.`

**Fix**

Use the expectation-errors setup and solver, or use the ordinary shock form.

codes.title: Learnt-in endval needs expectation-errors commands
codes.markdown:
### E423: Learnt-in endval needs expectation-errors commands

A nondefault `endval(learnt_in=…)` block needs both expectation-errors setup and solver, without regular perfect-foresight setup or solver. Dynare refuses: `the 'endval(learnt_in=…)' block can only be used in conjunction with the 'perfect_foresight_with_expectation_errors_setup' and 'perfect_foresight_with_expectation_errors_solver' commands.`

**Fix**

Use the expectation-errors setup and solver, or use ordinary `endval`.

codes.title: Learnt-in controlled paths need expectation-errors commands
codes.markdown:
### E424: Learnt-in controlled paths need expectation-errors commands

A nondefault `perfect_foresight_controlled_paths(learnt_in=…)` block needs both expectation-errors setup and solver, without regular perfect-foresight setup or solver. Dynare refuses: `the 'perfect_foresight_controlled_paths(learnt_in=…)' block can only be used in conjunction with the 'perfect_foresight_with_expectation_errors_setup' and 'perfect_foresight_with_expectation_errors_solver' commands.`

**Fix**

Use the expectation-errors setup and solver, or a default controlled-path block.

codes.title: Learnt-in shock paths need expectation-errors commands
codes.markdown:
### E425: Learnt-in shock paths need expectation-errors commands

A nondefault `shock_paths(learnt_in=…)` block needs both expectation-errors setup and solver, without regular perfect-foresight setup or solver. Dynare refuses: `the 'shock_paths(learnt_in=…)' block can only be used in conjunction with the 'perfect_foresight_with_expectation_errors_setup' and 'perfect_foresight_with_expectation_errors_solver' commands.`

**Fix**

Use the expectation-errors setup and solver, or a default shock-path block.

codes.title: Removed variable used in an expression
codes.markdown:
### E426: Removed variable used in an expression

An expression uses a variable after `model_remove` or `var_remove` changed its type to excluded. This includes planner objectives, Ramsey constraints, and steady-state RHS values. Dynare refuses: `Variable 'c' can no longer be used since it has been excluded by a previous 'model_remove' or 'var_remove' statement`. A use before the removal, or after a successful type restoration, is allowed.

**Warrant**

For a steady-state RHS, the range points at the written name and its excluded role is captured when the use is parsed, including repeated macro copies.

**Fix**

Keep the variable in the model, or stop using it after its removal.

codes.title: Subsample range name assigned twice
codes.markdown:
### E427: Subsample range name assigned twice

One `subsamples` declaration assigns the same range name twice. Dynare refuses: `Symbol s may only be assigned once in a SUBSAMPLE statement`. A second whole declaration is allowed.

**Fix**

Give each range in the declaration a distinct name.

codes.title: Subsample copy source is missing
codes.markdown:
### E428: Subsample copy source is missing

A `subsamples` copy names a source head with no earlier subsample declaration. Dynare refuses: `a does not have an associated subsample statement.`

**Fix**

Declare the source ranges before copying them.

codes.title: Named prior or options has no subsample declaration
codes.markdown:
### E429: Named prior or options has no subsample declaration

A named `prior` or `options` body refers to a head with no subsample declaration. Dynare refuses: `A subsample statement has not been issued for a`. The named copy forms do not run this lookup.

**Fix**

Declare the head's subsample ranges before the named prior or options body.

codes.title: Subsample range name was not declared
codes.markdown:
### E430: Subsample range name was not declared

A named `prior` or `options` body uses a range name absent from that head's subsample declaration. Dynare refuses: `The subsample name t was not previously declared in a subsample statement.`

**Fix**

Use one of the declared range names, or add the range to the subsample declaration.

codes.title: Subsample target has an invalid final symbol type
codes.markdown:
### E431: Subsample target has an invalid final symbol type

A `subsamples` declaration or copy has a target whose final type is neither parameter, plain exogenous, nor endogenous. Dynare accepts through its JSON checks but refuses when writing MATLAB files: `subsamples: invalid symbol type for d`. The first target name determines the type, including after `change_type` or `var_remove`.

**Fix**

Use a parameter, `varexo`, or `var` target, or change the target's final type.

codes.title: var(log) variable in a VAR, trend, or PAC equation
codes.markdown:
### E432: var(log) variable in a VAR, trend, or PAC equation

A selected VAR or trend-component equation, or an equation with pac_expectation, uses an endogenous declared with var(log). Dynare refuses at transform: `the following variables are declared with var(log) and therefore cannot appear in a VAR/TCM/PAC equation`.

**Fix**

Remove the log declaration for that variable or change the selected equation.

codes.title: Selected model equation tag is absent
codes.markdown:
### E433: Selected model equation tag is absent

A var_model or trend_component_model eqtags/targets list names no equation in the effective written model. Dynare refuses at transform: `looking for equation tag X failed.` or `no equation is named 'X'`. model_remove and model_replace affect which tags exist.

**Fix**

Use a present [name=] tag or restore the removed equation.

codes.title: VAR or trend-component equation has the wrong shape
codes.markdown:
### E434: VAR or trend-component equation has the wrong shape

A selected equation violates Dynare's LHS or RHS variable and timing rules, repeats an LHS, or uses a binary expression on the LHS. Dynare refuses at transform with the matching VAR or trend-component equation sentence. A structural VAR permits contemporaneous endogenous variables on the RHS.

This check uses the final symbol type after successful `change_type` statements, rather than the list where the name was declared.

**Fix**

Give each equation one untimed endogenous LHS and use only the allowed RHS timing.

codes.title: VAR expectation auxiliary model is absent
codes.markdown:
### E435: VAR expectation auxiliary model is absent

A var_expectation_model refers to an auxiliary_model_name that is neither a var_model nor a trend_component_model. Dynare refuses at transform: `var_expectation_model NAME refers to nonexistent auxiliary model AUX`.

**Fix**

Declare the named auxiliary model or correct the name.

codes.title: VAR expectation expression has the wrong linear form
codes.markdown:
### E436: VAR expectation expression has the wrong linear form

The variable/expression in var_expectation_model is not a linear combination of current endogenous variables in a written case that needs no rewrite. Dynare refuses at transform: `expression in var_expectation_model NAME is not of the expected form: ...`.

This check uses the final symbol type after successful `change_type` statements, rather than the list where the name was declared.

**Fix**

Use current endogenous variables with numeric or single-parameter coefficients.

codes.title: PAC options conflict with target information
codes.markdown:
### E437: PAC options conflict with target information

A pac_model gives growth, auxname, or kind while a matching pac_target_info block exists, or gives kind for a model-consistent-expectations PAC. Dynare refuses at check with the option-specific `for PAC model ... it is not possible ...` sentence.

**Fix**

Put target components in pac_target_info and remove the conflicting pac_model option.

codes.title: PAC target information is incomplete or inconsistent
codes.markdown:
### E438: PAC target information is incomplete or inconsistent

A pac_target_info block lacks a target, nonstationary auxiliary name, component auxname or kind; gives growth to a stationary kind ll component; or has no kind dd/dl component. Dynare refuses at check with the matching field sentence.

**Fix**

Complete each component and include a nonstationary one.

**Range warrant**

Missing target, nonstationary auxiliary, or nonstationary-component summaries select `pac_target_info`. A component missing `auxname` or `kind` selects its own `component` keyword. A stationary component with a present growth row keeps its existing range. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: Semi-structural command lacks a required option
codes.markdown:
### E439: Semi-structural command lacks a required option

A var_model, trend_component_model, var_expectation_model, or pac_model lacks one of its required options. Dynare refuses while parsing: `You must pass the 'OPTION' option to the 'COMMAND' statement.`

**Fix**

Add the required option to that command.

**Range warrant**

A missing required option selects the owning `var_model`, `trend_component_model`, `var_expectation_model`, or `pac_model` keyword. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: Semi-structural model name is repeated
codes.markdown:
### E440: Semi-structural model name is repeated

A second command of the same semi-structural model kind uses an earlier model_name. Dynare refuses while parsing: `a VAR model already exists with the name NAME`, with corresponding wording for the other three kinds.

**Fix**

Give the second model a distinct name or remove it.

codes.title: VAR expectation needs one expression source
codes.markdown:
### E441: VAR expectation needs one expression source

var_expectation_model needs either variable or expression, and rejects both together. Dynare refuses while parsing with the corresponding `You must pass either` or `You can't pass both` sentence.

**Fix**

Keep exactly one of variable and expression.

**Range warrant**

When both `variable` and `expression` are absent, the range selects `var_expectation_model`. When both are present, it keeps the existing range. The keyword excludes options, body, and `end`. If its written file or token cannot be verified, the previous mapped range remains.

codes.title: VAR expectation discount has the wrong type
codes.markdown:
### E442: VAR expectation discount has the wrong type

A var_expectation_model discount is neither a constant expression nor a parameter. Dynare refuses while parsing: `The discount factor must be a constant expression or a parameter`.

**Fix**

Use a numeric constant or declared parameter.

codes.title: VAR expectation time shift is positive
codes.markdown:
### E443: VAR expectation time shift is positive

Dynare refuses a positive var_expectation_model time_shift while parsing: `The 'time_shift' option must be a non-positive integer`.

**Fix**

Use zero or a negative integer.

codes.title: PAC discount is not a parameter
codes.markdown:
### E444: PAC discount is not a parameter

The pac_model discount names a declared non-parameter symbol. Dynare refuses while parsing: `NAME is not a parameter`.

**Fix**

Use a declared parameter.

codes.title: Named VAR or PAC operator inside epilogue
codes.markdown:
### E445: Named VAR or PAC operator inside epilogue

Dynare refuses var_expectation, pac_expectation, and pac_target_nonstationary inside epilogue while parsing: `The 'OPERATOR' operator is forbidden in 'epilogue'.` The model block can contain these operators.

**Fix**

Remove the operator from epilogue or move the calculation into a model equation.

codes.title: PAC auxiliary model name is absent
codes.markdown:
### E446: PAC auxiliary model name is absent

A pac_model auxiliary_model_name names no var_model or trend_component_model. Dynare refuses at transform: `aux_model_name not recognized as VAR model or Trend Component model`.

**Fix**

Declare the named auxiliary model or correct the name.

codes.title: VAR expectation operator names no model
codes.markdown:
### E447: VAR expectation operator names no model

A model equation uses var_expectation(NAME) without a matching var_expectation_model. Dynare refuses at transform: `unknown model 'NAME' used in var_expectation expression`.

**Fix**

Declare a var_expectation_model with that model_name or correct the call.

codes.title: PAC growth has a nonlinear written product
codes.markdown:
### E448: PAC growth has a nonlinear written product

A PAC growth expression directly multiplies two variables, so Dynare refuses at transform: `PAC growth must be a linear combination of variables`. Other growth forms may need rewrite before this check.

This check uses the final symbol type after successful `change_type` statements, rather than the list where the name was declared.

**Fix**

Use a linear combination of variables and constants for growth.

codes.title: PAC model has no expectation equation
codes.markdown:
### E449: PAC model has no expectation equation

A pac_model has no effective written equation using its pac_expectation(NAME) operator. Dynare refuses at transform: `the model does not contain the 'pac_expectation(NAME)' operator.`

**Fix**

Use the named operator in a model equation, or remove the unused pac_model.

codes.title: PAC expectation appears in several equations
codes.markdown:
### E450: PAC expectation appears in several equations

Two effective written equations use pac_expectation(NAME) for the same PAC model. Dynare refuses at transform: `It is not possible to use 'pac_expectation(NAME)' in several equations.` Two calls in one equation are accepted.

**Fix**

Keep that PAC expectation in one equation.

codes.title: PAC expectation names no PAC model
codes.markdown:
### E451: PAC expectation names no PAC model

A written model equation uses pac_expectation(NAME) without a matching pac_model. Dynare refuses at transform: `the pac_expectation operator references an unknown pac_model`.

**Fix**

Declare the named pac_model or correct the operator name.

codes.title: Nonstationary PAC target cannot be matched
codes.markdown:
### E452: Nonstationary PAC target cannot be matched

A written model equation uses pac_target_nonstationary(NAME) when the named pac_model or pac_target_info block is missing. Dynare refuses at transform: `the pac_target_nonstationary operator does not match a corresponding 'pac_target_info' block`.

**Fix**

Add the missing PAC model or target-info block, or correct the operator name.

codes.title: PAC growth correction name conflicts with a declaration
codes.markdown:
### E453: PAC growth correction name conflicts with a declaration

A written declaration uses the name NAME_pac_growth_neutrality_correction generated by a pac_model growth option. Dynare refuses at transform with its growth-neutrality correction conflict sentence.

**Fix**

Rename the declared symbol.

codes.title: MCE PAC parameter name conflicts with a declaration
codes.markdown:
### E454: MCE PAC parameter name conflicts with a declaration

A written declaration uses the first mce_alpha_NAME_1 parameter generated for a model-consistent-expectations PAC. Dynare refuses at transform with its generated-parameter conflict sentence.

**Fix**

Rename the declared symbol.

codes.title: Backward or component PAC parameter name conflicts
codes.markdown:
### E455: Backward or component PAC parameter name conflicts

A written declaration uses a fixed backward-VAR constant or component growth-correction parameter name generated by a PAC model. Dynare refuses at transform with its auxiliary-parameter conflict sentence. Lag-indexed names need the rewritten model and remain silent.

**Fix**

Rename the declared symbol.

codes.title: PAC expectation auxiliary name conflicts
codes.markdown:
### E456: PAC expectation auxiliary name conflicts

A written declaration uses an auxiliary variable name generated for pac_expectation, or a PAC component/model auxname reuses a target or expectation auxiliary name generated earlier, including by another PAC model. Dynare refuses at transform with its generated-variable conflict sentence.

**Fix**

Give each auxiliary a distinct name and keep those names free of declared symbols.

codes.title: PAC nonstationary target auxiliary name conflicts
codes.markdown:
### E457: PAC nonstationary target auxiliary name conflicts

A written declaration or previously generated PAC auxiliary uses the auxname_target_nonstationary of a PAC target-info block. Dynare refuses at transform with its pac_target_nonstationary generated-variable conflict sentence.

**Fix**

Give the nonstationary target a distinct auxiliary name.

codes.title: PAC target expression has no defining equation
codes.markdown:
### E458: PAC target expression has no defining equation

A direct target product such as v*v has no matching left-hand side in the effective written model. Dynare refuses at transform: `there is no equation whose LHS is equal to the 'target' of 'pac_target_info(NAME)'`. Other target expressions may depend on rewrite and stay silent.

**Fix**

Make target match an equation left-hand side, or use the intended target variable.

codes.title: Unknown heterogeneity dimension
codes.markdown:
### E459: Unknown heterogeneity dimension

A ``var``, ``varexo``, ``parameters``, ``model``, or ``shocks`` option names a heterogeneity dimension that was not declared. Dynare refuses: `Unknown heterogeneity dimension: ghost`.

**Fix**

Declare the dimension with ``heterogeneity_dimension``, or correct the name.

codes.title: Heterogeneity dimension declared twice
codes.markdown:
### E460: Heterogeneity dimension declared twice

The same heterogeneity dimension name is declared again. Dynare refuses: `Heterogeneity dimension 'd' already declared`.

**Fix**

Keep one declaration of that name.

codes.title: Heterogeneous symbol in planner_objective
codes.markdown:
### E461: Heterogeneous symbol in planner_objective

``planner_objective`` uses a heterogeneous variable or parameter. Dynare refuses: `Symbol 'a' cannot be used in 'planner_objective', because it is heterogeneous.`

**Fix**

Use an aggregate variable in the planner objective.

codes.title: Heterogeneous symbol in occbin_constraints
codes.markdown:
### E462: Heterogeneous symbol in occbin_constraints

``occbin_constraints`` uses a heterogeneous variable or parameter. Dynare refuses: `Symbol 'a' cannot be used in 'occbin_constraints', because it is heterogeneous.`

**Fix**

Use an aggregate variable in the constraint.

codes.title: Heterogeneous symbol outside the model
codes.markdown:
### E463: Heterogeneous symbol outside the model

A heterogeneous variable or parameter is used outside a model declaration. Dynare refuses: `Symbol 'a' cannot be used outside model declaration, because it is heterogeneous.`

**Fix**

Use the name inside its ``model(heterogeneity=…)`` block, or aggregate it with ``SUM``.

codes.title: Heterogeneous symbol in the epilogue
codes.markdown:
### E464: Heterogeneous symbol in the epilogue

The ``epilogue`` block uses a heterogeneous variable or parameter. Dynare refuses: `Symbol 'a' cannot be used in epilogue block, because it is heterogeneous.`

**Fix**

Use an aggregate variable in the epilogue.

codes.title: Heterogeneous shock variance on the wrong type
codes.markdown:
### E465: Heterogeneous shock variance on the wrong type

A ``shocks(heterogeneity=…)`` block sets a variance on a name that is not a heterogeneous exogenous variable. Dynare refuses: `shocks: setting a variance on 'y' is not allowed, because it is not a heterogeneous exogenous variable`.

**Fix**

Set the variance on a ``varexo(heterogeneity=…)`` name.

codes.title: Heterogeneous shock standard error on the wrong type
codes.markdown:
### E466: Heterogeneous shock standard error on the wrong type

A ``shocks(heterogeneity=…)`` block sets a standard error on a name that is not a heterogeneous exogenous variable. Dynare refuses: `shocks: setting a standard error on 'y' is not allowed, because it is not a heterogeneous exogenous variable`.

**Fix**

Set the standard error on a ``varexo(heterogeneity=…)`` name.

codes.title: Heterogeneous shock covariance on the wrong type
codes.markdown:
### E467: Heterogeneous shock covariance on the wrong type

A ``shocks(heterogeneity=…)`` covariance names something other than heterogeneous exogenous variables. Dynare refuses: `shocks: setting a covariance between 'y' and 'e'is not allowed; covariances can only be specified for heterogeneous exogenous variables`.

**Fix**

Name two ``varexo(heterogeneity=…)`` variables.

codes.title: Heterogeneous shock correlation on the wrong type
codes.markdown:
### E468: Heterogeneous shock correlation on the wrong type

A ``shocks(heterogeneity=…)`` correlation names something other than heterogeneous exogenous variables. Dynare refuses: `shocks: setting a correlation between 'y' and 'e'is not allowed; covariances can only be specified for heterogeneous exogenous variables`.

**Fix**

Name two ``varexo(heterogeneity=…)`` variables.

codes.title: Lagged heterogeneous exogenous variable
codes.markdown:
### E469: Lagged heterogeneous exogenous variable

A heterogeneous model equation lags a heterogeneous exogenous variable. Dynare refuses: `In model(heterogeneity=d), equation 1: lagged heterogeneous exogenous variable 'eh' is not supported.`

**Fix**

Use the shock contemporaneously.

codes.title: Lead on a heterogeneous exogenous variable
codes.markdown:
### E470: Lead on a heterogeneous exogenous variable

A heterogeneous model equation leads a heterogeneous exogenous variable. Dynare refuses: `In model(heterogeneity=d), equation 1: lead on heterogeneous exogenous variable 'eh(+1)' is not supported.`

**Fix**

Use the shock contemporaneously.

codes.title: Heterogeneous endogenous lag beyond -1
codes.markdown:
### E471: Heterogeneous endogenous lag beyond -1

A heterogeneous endogenous variable is lagged by more than one period. Dynare refuses: `In model(heterogeneity=d), equation 1: heterogeneous endogenous variable 'a' with lag -2 is not supported (maximum lag is -1).`

**Fix**

Keep the lag at ``-1`` or contemporaneous.

codes.title: Heterogeneous endogenous lead beyond +1
codes.markdown:
### E472: Heterogeneous endogenous lead beyond +1
